routing.reason: A small feature in one small codebase (migration, API validation, a date field on the page, tests, README) with testable acceptance criteria already written.
rulings: Ruling: default workflow, not hotfix — it is a feature, not an urgent fix — cost if wrong: none, the plan gate only adds a short pause

Ruling: skip `frame` (po) — the ticket already lists six testable acceptance criteria — cost if wrong: an edge case such as a past due date or date-only comparison is missed; low, since the ticket scopes it to storing and showing the date

Ruling: skip `prd`, `architecture`, `ux` and `seo` — not a vague epic, one module's design (src/db.ts, src/tasks.ts, src/app.ts), the page only gains a date input and a label, and there are no public pages — cost if wrong: the date field's look or labelling needs a small follow-up
Ruling: `plan` at low effort — one small codebase, about five files — cost if wrong: a task split that is too coarse

Ruling: `security` at medium effort — it parses user input into SQL (the date validation) but touches no authentication, payments or personal data — cost if wrong: a validation bypass slips through; the prepared statements and the strict date check limit this
Ruling: no squads — the project declares none — cost if wrong: none

Ruling: validation must reject real-calendar-invalid days such as 2026-02-30 (an exact round-trip check, not only a regex) and the migration must be appended as a new entry after the shipped one in src/db.ts, never edited into it — the ticket requires both (criteria 3 and 4) — cost if wrong: invalid dates are stored, or existing databases break

Ruling: budget $1.50 — covers the plan, one or two implementation tasks, checks, the code review rounds, the database review of the migration, the security review and the visual review — cost if wrong: the run stops before its reviews; the user can raise it

criteria.why: Task and Row gain due_date, toTask normalises it to null, and the column is nullable with no default.
POST passes the parsed due_date through. PATCH sets it, clears it with null, and keeps it when the key is undefined.

parseDueDate checks the regex and then a UTC round-trip. It throws a ValidationError that maps to 400 with the exact message before any write. The tests cover this. Years 0000–0099 are wrongly rejected, which is a minor gap.
A second migration, ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN due_date TEXT, is added. A test migrates a version-1 database and checks that old rows get null.
The page renders a <time> element after the title when due_date is set, and the add form has an optional date input.
Tests cover default, create, patch, invalid values and migration. The README documents the field, the 400 error and the migration.

findings.what: The unrelated line `const filter =document.querySelector(...)` was reformatted and lost a space. It is a stray style regression.
The submit handler now has a try/catch that shows errors. This is reasonable, because a 400 would otherwise be an unhandled rejection, but it goes slightly beyond the ticket.
Date.UTC maps years 0–99 to 1900–1999, so valid strings such as 0050-01-01 are rejected. This is negligible in practice.
The test imports `migrate` from src/db.ts, but the diff does not show it being exported. The test file fails to load if it was not already exported.
PATCH validates due_date before looking up the task. An invalid date on a missing id returns 400 instead of 404. This is acceptable.

judge.summary: The implementation meets every criterion with a small, clean change: strict date validation, a proper migration, a UI field and thorough tests, including a migration test. The only faults are an unrelated formatting slip in app.js, a test import of `migrate` that may not be exported, and an edge case for years below 100.
